1	# Claudinite — the canon's own non-portable working rules
2	
3	This is the Claudinite home repo's own local pack: the capture surface for lessons that are
4	**specific to working on the canon itself** and would not make sense mounted into a consuming
5	project. Portable lessons — anything true for repos beyond this one — belong in the shared canon
6	under `packs/`/`skills/` instead (proposed by PR, or lifted by the promote stage).
7	
8	The growth lifecycle writes here automatically: the `growth-extract` and `conversation-extract`
9	daily tasks route the canon's own non-portable lessons into this pack (each at the local
10	promotion ladder's strongest mechanism — a check where the rule is deterministic, otherwise terse
11	prose below).
12	
13	## Standing owner decisions — settled, do not re-litigate
14	
15	- **`canon-curation` lives in `.claudinite/local/packs/`, not `packs/`** (owner decision,
16	  2026-07-19). The canon home's curation duties are Claudinite-maintaining-Claudinite —
17	  project-specific content on the home's own capture surface. Do not propose moving it back, and
18	  do not describe the move as open or provisional.
19	- **Local-pack `run_daily` scheduling is ON — the fleet's default path** (same decision). The
20	  planner reads every member's local-pack daily descriptors by default; never reintroduce an
21	  "experimental / not enabled" framing or an opt-in seam for it.
22	- **Packs-tree segregation is barriers configuration only.** Any rule about what the `packs/`
23	  tree may reference is expressed by declaring/configuring the `barriers` pack (contributed
24	  edges, `siblings`/`scope` capabilities — extend barriers generically if a capability is
25	  missing). Never write standalone code that checks packs-tree segregation.
26	- **A `docs/<initiative>/DESIGN.md` records the mechanism only** (owner decision, 2026-07-23,
27	  #420). Status, phase tracking, in-flight-PR reconciliation and remaining work live in that
28	  initiative's tracking issue (agent-preprocessing → #394); a phased plan lives in the sibling
29	  `MIGRATION.md`. Don't reintroduce a status / open-questions / remaining-work section there.
30	- **Multi-session work hands off through the tracking issue, never a prepared prompt** (owner
31	  correction, 2026-07-23). The owner's opener is `continue work on #<n>`, so state not written
32	  into the issue is lost. Before ending a session on unfinished work, update the issue and let
33	  the session summary be a pointer to it — never compose a bespoke "pick up from here" prompt.
34	- **The canon never knows which repos consume it — fleet-wide aggregation is Sheepdog's domain**
35	  (owner correction, 2026-07-28, #520). Designing anything that spans repos, the tempting shape is
36	  a member list (or a "fleet" task) living in the canon. It doesn't go here: the canon carries only
37	  **mechanisms exercised on itself**, and the knowledge of *which* repos exist stays in the
38	  **Sheepdog** repo and its pack, which enumerates members at runtime from its own
39	  `.claudinite-checks.json` entry — exactly where `fleet-census` and `fleet-freshness` already keep
40	  it. So a cross-repo feature splits in two: a self-contained per-repo half in the canon, and the
41	  aggregation half as a Sheepdog fleet task. **No repo list exists anywhere in canon code** — and a
42	  derived fleet artifact lands in Sheepdog as a daily **auto-merged PR of a `GENERATED` file**,
43	  never a direct commit to its `main`.
44	- **A pack default stays in the pack — don't ask it at adoption, don't write it into a member's
45	  config** (owner ruling, 2026-07-28, #527/#528). An adoption question whose recommended answer is
46	  right for nearly everyone is "bad noise": it taxes every adopting repo to re-state the default,
47	  and materializing that answer into `.claudinite-checks.json` freezes a copy that then drifts from
48	  the pack and has to be migrated. Keep the default in the pack's own code, ask nothing, and let the
49	  rare project that wants to differ add the setting by hand. Read config as *optional* — an unset
50	  key means "the default", never "misconfigured" (`retention_days` unset is precisely why the
51	  conversation-extract prune is skipped rather than failing).
52	
53	## Canon-specific gotchas
54	
55	- **Baselining backfill skips the home.** The nightly baselining that lands a `seededByDefault`
56	  pack (and canon-delivered declaration changes) on every member is gated `!isHome`, so the canon
57	  home is the one repo it never reaches: what the fleet receives automatically, this repo's own
58	  `.claudinite-checks.json` only ever gets by hand.
59	- **The home doesn't declare `git-github`, so its skills never mount — never conclude "no such
60	  skill" from `.claude/skills/`.** `mount-skills.mjs` filters on the *literal* declaration
61	  (`isActive(p, { packs: declared })`), not the `requires` closure `check_the_world.mjs` resolves,
62	  and the baselining that would normalize that closure into `.claudinite-checks.json` is the one
63	  thing gated `!isHome` — so `merge-to-main` and `git-github-advanced` are simply absent here.
64	  Read `packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` out of the tracked tree — the corpus *is* this repo,
65	  and an unmounted skill says nothing about whether its procedure applies. The seeding gap above
66	  is a different one (`git-github` arrives by closure, never `seededByDefault`); catching this
67	  one needs `resolveDeclaredPacks` compared against the literal declaration.
68	- **Never re-serialize a repo's JSON config to apply an edit — patch the text.** A round-trip
69	  rewrites what it wasn't asked to: Python's `json.dump` defaults to `ensure_ascii=True` (every
70	  non-ASCII character becomes a `\uXXXX` escape), and indent, key order and the trailing newline
71	  become the serializer's opinion. Nothing fails and tests stay green, so it rides onward. Edit
72	  JSON as anchored text; if you must round-trip, pin every lossy default and read the resulting
73	  diff before committing. (Portable — a promote candidate for `repo-text-sweeps`, where a
74	  `\uXXXX`-in-tracked-JSON check would carry it.)
75	- **Test git fixtures must commit with signing off.** `engine-tests/helpers.mjs`'s `makeRepo`
76	  overrides identity but not signing, so all 31 call sites route fixture commits through the
77	  signing service; when it degrades, each commit blocks on it and the suite leaks descriptors
78	  (~800 per full run against a 4096 cap) until `git commit` and `git push` fail process-wide.
79	  Commit with `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit --no-gpg-sign`: signing a tmpdir throwaway
80	  buys nothing. (Portable — a promote candidate for `writing-tests`.)
81	- **A canon session with a consumer repo also in its sources will reach for the *consumer's*
82	  merge skill — merge by the skill of the repo you are merging into.** Canon work is routinely
83	  dual-repo (the canon plus the fleet member being piloted), and both repos ship a merge skill
84	  under different names — the canon's `packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/` and, say, GCEC's
85	  local `merge-and-ci`. The consumer's skill wins the match on name/description and is followed
86	  to the letter, so the canon-only steps in *its* recipe are silently skipped — repeatedly, the
87	  **post-merge conversation capture** (`node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue
88	  <n>`, the "After the merge" section of `merge-to-main`). So: before merging in a dual-repo
89	  session, resolve the merge skill **by target repo**, not by which skill matched first — and
90	  treat capture as part of the merge, not as an optional epilogue.
91	- **Fail-soft SessionStart steps hide their own breakage fleet-wide — test the emitted
92	  output, not the exit code.** Every `engine/pack_loader/` SessionStart step
93	  (`inject-pack-prose.mjs`, `mount-skills.mjs`, `env-requirements.mjs`) wraps its body in
94	  `try { ... } catch {}` so a broken loader never blocks a session. That fail-soft is deliberate,
95	  but it means a runtime fault — a wrong dynamic-import target, a renamed module — exits 0 and
96	  simply emits nothing: no error, no signal. And because the engine is vendored verbatim into
97	  every member, one canon regression silently disables that step across the whole fleet at once.
98	  So a step like this must be guarded by a regression test that runs the real script against a
99	  real corpus and asserts the **positive** effect — prose IS emitted — never merely that
100	  `status === 0` (which fail-soft makes meaningless); see
101	  `engine-tests/pack_loader/inject-pack-prose.test.mjs`.
102	- **The nightly self-refresh cannot repair the vendor-set computation — pin operational
103	  files against the REAL canon tree.** Baselining's converge re-runs
104	  `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs` from canon HEAD, so a bug *in that computation* is
105	  the one class of canon regression that is not self-healing: every refresh faithfully
106	  reproduces it, and recovery is an out-of-band vendor refresh applied to each member by
107	  hand. So when the vendor set excludes by *pattern*, an operational file that matches
108	  needs a by-path whitelist (`VENDORED_ENGINE_DOCS`) **and** a regression test asserting
109	  against the real canon tree, not only a synthetic fixture: a fixture keeps proving the
110	  whitelist mechanism works while the live path silently drops out from under it (see the
111	  paired tests in `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.test.mjs`).
112	- **A check that selects its inputs by path pattern can reach zero files and still pass — assert
113	  the live in-scope count.** When skills moved inside their owning pack (#385),
114	  `skill-no-enforcement-narration` kept scanning the root-level `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` layout: it
115	  matched nothing in any tree, read as live, and caught nothing until a human noticed the prose it
116	  should have flagged (#560 — 21 skills in scope once repointed). Its fixtures are why it hid so
117	  well; they spelled the same dead layout, so five green tests proved the *matching* and never the
118	  *selection*. A scan-based check therefore needs one assertion over the **real** tree that its
119	  scope is non-empty. Other half of the same class: agent-facing text pointing where the code isn't
120	  — the same PR fixed a rule whose `why`, fix text and `doc` all named `engine/checks_helpers` or
121	  `checks/lib`, neither of which ever existed. Nothing catches that on its own —
122	  `reference-integrity` is work-scoped and flags only paths the branch itself deletes — so grep the
123	  tree for any directory you name in a finding, a remedy, or a doc pointer before shipping it.
124	- **A scheduled task's precondition gates on movement in the window, never on standing state.** "An
125	  open PR exists" is true forever once it is true once, so the task wakes every night, spends an
126	  agent, and re-derives yesterday's verdict over an unchanged set (three of tidy-repo's tasks
127	  shipped that way; fixed in #554). Gate on the objects' own movement — a `touched` list or a
128	  tip-commit date, which the signal collector has to actually carry (`branches` carried names only,
129	  so "is any of this new" had no answer at all). A signal that is true most days on an active repo
130	  — a substantive `main` move — may only **widen** an already-triggered run, never wake one. And the
131	  gate is not the scope: where a verdict is relative to the rest of the set (superseded-by,
132	  already-in-`main`), newness gates and the full set stays the scope. (Portable — a promote
133	  candidate for `basics/scheduled-tasks.md`, which states the precondition contract but not this.)
134	- **You cannot force a due slot by running the scheduler workflow by hand.** Dueness is
135	  stateless — a slot is due iff its time falls in `(last successful run, now]` — so a
136	  `workflow_dispatch` run outside the slot's window succeeds, prints `- no tasks due`, and
137	  does nothing. It looks like a healthy run. To exercise a task Action-side, invoke its
138	  worker directly, or move the slot hour in `taskScheduler` and wait for the cron.
139	- **A scheduled task is gated twice — prove a change through `planRun`, never through its own
140	  precondition.** `planRun` computes the due list *before* any precondition runs, so a task whose
141	  most-recent slot has already been run is never evaluated and never reads its signals at all. #513's
142	  forced-run override landed with every test driving the precondition (or the signal collector) directly
143	  and was inert on exactly the run it existed for — the mid-day manual trigger — because the due-list
144	  gate it never touched had already dropped the task (`evaluations: []`; fixed in #516). A test that
145	  starts *inside* the gate proves only "works once evaluated" and says nothing about whether the task
146	  ever gets there. Drive the real `planRun` from a deliberately **non-due** slot: that is the only shape
147	  that catches it.
148	- **Every due task in a run shares ONE checkout — an agentless worker must not touch it.** The
149	  scheduler runs the whole due list in a single working tree, so a worker that checks out a branch or
150	  leaves an index behind hands the next task a tree it did not expect, and a run that dies leaves the
151	  mess for whatever follows. A task whose output is a regenerated file lands it through
152	  `engine/scheduler/deliver-generated.mjs` — git plumbing against the fetched base tip, with HEAD, the
153	  index and the working tree untouched — and reads its prior state from that base rather than local
154	  HEAD, so stacked runs stay idempotent. (`basics/baselining`'s own deliver is the deliberate
155	  exception: it commits a whole working tree under the member's delivery preference.)
156	- **A code-search hit is evidence; a code-search miss is not — survey by reading each file.**
157	- **Derive the test file list from the tree — every hand-written glob here under-runs the suite.**
158	  There is no `package.json` and no test script, so each session invents its own incantation and
159	  silently verifies less than it thinks. Measured in this checkout: `node --test <dir>` does not
160	  recurse — it resolves the path as a module and dies with `Cannot find module`; bash `**` is not
161	  recursive without `globstar`, so `engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs` reaches
162	  **37 of 65** tracked test files. Four consecutive sessions (2026-07-26, #459/#452/#435/#468) each
163	  wrote a different command and reported 587, 690, 621 and 697 tests — three of them pushed after
164	  running a strict subset. Neither published list is authoritative either: `ci.yml`'s `tests=(…)`
165	  array omits `vendoring/*.test.mjs`, and `engine/checks/README.md`'s "as CI runs it" one-liner
166	  names `engine/test/`, `skills/` and `mount/`, none of which exist. So enumerate from git and let
167	  the count speak: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`. (The drift-guard, once the array is
168	  clean: assert every tracked `*.test.mjs` is matched by `ci.yml`'s globs.)
169	- **A branch that waited overnight has lost its base *and* possibly its premise — re-verify the
170	  problem still exists on current `main`, unasked.** This repo merges its own scheduled-task PRs
171	  without a human, on top of multi-phase migrations that retire whole directories: measured on
172	  PR #465, `main` moved **14 commits in 13.7 hours** and one of them (#473, "retire `run_daily/`")
173	  *deleted the file the PR's diagnosis rested on* and had already landed most of its content. The
174	  branch rebased cleanly and the tests stayed green — the change was simply no longer the change to
175	  make, and the correct move was `git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` and re-applying only the
176	  surviving slice (9 files → 2). So syncing the base is not the check; the check is a **content**
177	  one: after `git fetch`, read what the new commits did to the surface you are changing and state
178	  whether the problem is still there, what the goal was, and what survives. Do this whenever you
179	  return to a paused branch, before presenting it — the owner should never have to ask "is this
180	  change still needed" (asked three times on #465 before it was volunteered).
181	- **Every `Claude_Code_Remote` call costs minutes, and a call that returns nothing has NOT failed —
182	  never re-issue it.** The whole server behaves this way, not one tool: measured over four sessions
183	  on 2026-07-29, `add_repo` ran 270–285s a call, `send_later` 117–390s, `list_triggers` 139–325s,
184	  `delete_trigger` 286–301s, `subscribe_pr_activity` 14–237s. They read like cheap registrations,
185	  so a session issues one, sits through minutes of silence, concludes it hung, and issues it again —
186	  and *the duplicate is the dominant cost*, because the first call had already succeeded:
187	  **#562 (`2026-07-29T1500Z`) — 6 `add_repo` calls, 1121s of that session's 1391s of tool
188	  wall-clock (81%)**, with `HelloWorldFlutterApp` added twice (285s + 271s); **#553
189	  (`2026-07-29T2206Z`) — the same PR check-in `send_later`d 4 times, 1107s of 2028s (55%)**; **#544
190	  (`2026-07-29T1248Z`) — `list_triggers` ×2, `delete_trigger` ×2 on one trigger id, `send_later` ×2:
191	  1854s of 2472s (75%)**, in a session whose real work was 166 tool calls. `AskUserQuestion` shares
192	  the shape — #559's session asked one question twice for 218s + 204s. So: **one call per intent,
193	  ever**, and when what you want is "is it green yet", read the check status directly and merge on
194	  the already-green result rather than buying a notification. Budget these calls before making them:
195	  four of them is most of an hour.
196	- **Sync local `main` with `git reset --hard origin/main`, never `git pull` — this repo's session
197	  clones are shallow.** The post-merge sync step of `merge-to-main` is where it bites, and it bit
198	  five separate sessions on 2026-07-29 alone (#548, #551, #537, #559 and the session-end capture of
199	  `73a4db48`). A shallow clone has no common ancestor with the fetched remote, so `git pull` either
200	  demands an explicit strategy or reports the stale local ref as carrying unique commits it does not
201	  have — and the tempting reading, "local `main` has work the remote lacks", is wrong every time:
202	  the session's own work is already *in* `origin/main`, which is why it just merged. #537's session
203	  spent 87s across `git pull`, `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` and log comparisons proving
204	  that from scratch; #559's landed on "git sees no common ancestor" the same way. Nothing of value
205	  is ever on this repo's local `main`, so the sync is unconditional: `git fetch origin main && git
206	  reset --hard origin/main`. (Portable — a promote candidate for `git-github`'s merge procedure,
207	  where "your clone may be shallow" is true of any container-hosted session.)
208	- **The home has no `.claudinite/shared/` mount — machinery paths must accept both roots.** A
209	  consumer runs the vendored engine under `.claudinite/shared/engine/…` with packs under
210	  `.claudinite/(shared|local)/packs/…`; the home *is* the corpus and runs the same code from the
211	  repo root. So a path, regex, or workflow command written to the consumer mount shape works
212	  fleet-wide and fails on exactly this repo — the last place anyone exercises it, so the break
213	  surfaces late. Write the two-root form up front: make the `.claudinite/(shared|local)/` prefix
214	  optional in a pattern, and in a command probe for `.claudinite/shared/` first, falling back to
215	  the repo root.

1	# canon-curation
2	
3	Claudinite's own curation duties — the fleet-facing work only **Claudinite** runs: promoting
4	members' lessons into the shared canon, sweeping the fleet's stacks for technologies the canon does
5	not yet home, and policing the corpus's `packs/` tree. (The
6	prose-to-checks backlog sweep is no longer canon-only — it moved to
7	[grow_with_claudinite](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) as a per-repo task with a
8	`pack_paths` config, so every repo sweeps its own packs and Claudinite also its core `packs/`.) A
9	**local pack** of the canon home
10	(`.claudinite/local/packs/`, by owner decision 2026-07-19: Claudinite-maintaining-Claudinite is
11	project-specific content, so it lives on the home's own capture surface, not in the portable
12	canon): `detect: null`, never seeded by `--init` or any migration, declared by hand in exactly one
13	repo — the canon home itself, as `local/canon-curation`. Its `tasks/<name>/` folders are found by
14	the home repo's own scheduler exactly like a canon pack's.
15	
16	**Declaration cardinality is the mechanism.** A pack's tasks run once per *declaring* repo, so a
17	pack only the home repo declares yields exactly one dispatch per task per slot — "central, once"
18	with no bespoke orchestrator step. Un-declaring the pack freezes canon absorption without touching
19	the members' side ([grow_with_claudinite](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md)).
20	
21	| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `growth-promote` | a participating member changed its local packs in the window | a PR against Claudinite's `main` |
24	| `growth-discover-packs` | weekly, over every covered member | a PR against Claudinite's `main` |
25	| `migrations-retire` | a fully-applied migration record has passed its TTL | a PR against Claudinite's `main` |
26	
27	| Rule (≤5 words) | How enforced |
28	|---|---|
29	| Pack prose: no enforcement narration | check `pack-no-enforcement-narration` |
30	| Packs import only own + engine | contributed barrier `pack-independence` ([pack-independence.mjs](pack-independence.mjs) — pure data; the [barriers pack](../../../../packs/barriers/README.md) builds the rule) |
31	
32	- **[tasks/growth-promote/](tasks/growth-promote/task.md)** — the growth lifecycle's central stage: read the changed members'
33	  local packs, **generalize** the portable lessons, route each to the right canon home, and open a
34	  PR for the owner to approve. When a portable lesson's technology has no pack home, it mints a
35	  fingerprinted **stub pack** (in its own dedicated PR). This is the sole judgment gate before
36	  shared canon.
37	- **[tasks/growth-discover-packs/](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)** — the weekly **fleet sweep** for
38	  technologies the canon does not yet home: read every member's stack, fold the members into one view
39	  (so first-sight dedup is free — the third member using a technology is the same gap as the first),
40	  and open an owner-reviewed PR authoring the missing `packs/<tech>/`. Its per-repo namesake in
41	  [grow_with_claudinite](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)
42	  is the other side of that line — it authors a repo's own **local** packs and may never re-create what
43	  a canon pack homes, so only this task can close a canon gap. (Promote's stub-minting is narrower
44	  still: one lesson's technology, minted as a seed; this task authors from the whole fleet's usage.)
45	- **[item-routing.md](item-routing.md)** — the shared worthiness + routing method promote (and an
46	  owner-requested retrospective pass) defers to, so every decision about admitting and placing an
47	  item is made the same way.
48	- **[promote-scope.mjs](promote-scope.mjs)** — the CI write-surface gate on promote's PRs: promote
49	  may write only under `packs/` and `skills/` (keyed on the `growth-promote` branch prefix).
50	
51	## The growth lifecycle — three independent stages, no barriers
52	
53	How a lesson is learned in a consuming project, lifted into the shared canon when it's portable,
54	and pruned back out of the project once the canon owns it. Two packs split it by who declares them:
55	**[grow_with_claudinite](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md)** (member-side: extract + dedup + pack
56	discovery, seeded, opt-out by removal) and **canon-curation** (this pack, the central stage).
57	
58	```
59	EXTRACT   per member    → auto-merging PR against the member's main   (grow_with_claudinite)
60	PROMOTE   central, once → PR against Claudinite's main                (canon-curation)
61	DEDUP     per member    → PR against the member's main                (grow_with_claudinite)
62	```
63	
64	All three are ordinary, **independent** planner units — there is no barrier and no phase ordering.
65	Each stage reads only what is already **merged**: promote processes whatever sits on members' mains
66	when it runs, so a lesson extracted tonight is promoted **tomorrow** night (the extract PR's merge
67	shows up in the next night's local-pack signal), and reaches other members' dedup once the promote PR
68	is approved and merged. That approval was always the dominant latency, so the barrier machinery bought little;
69	if the cadence ever matters, promote can run more often (twice daily, or before and after the
70	nightly) without any design change.
71	
72	**Review gates by blast radius, not uniformly.** Promote opens a PR — it's the sole judgment gate
73	before the shared canon every repo reads, so it always needs a human eye. Dedup opens a PR too — a
74	wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson. Extract lands through an **auto-merging PR** against the
75	member's `main` — it writes only that project's own local packs, so it earns a CI gate and a PR trail
76	but not a human reviewer; auto-merge keeps the fleet's daily lesson-capture from flooding review
77	requests. (An owner-requested, in-session retrospective delivers a PR for a human to review — see
78	[extracting-lessons.md](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/extracting-lessons.md).)
79	
80	**Central execution, no plumbing.** Promote runs from the Claudinite home repo with a fleet-wide
81	token, so it reads every participating member and opens its canon PR directly here — no
82	consumer-side Action, no cross-repo PAT, no labelled-issue up-path. The planner hands its gate the
83	`fleetMembers` aggregate (which members changed, and what they declare), and the gate hands the
84	worker the changed participants as `targets`.
85	
86	The session-scoped sibling of this nightly lifecycle — mining a single working session for lessons
87	— lives with [the growth pack's extracting-lessons method](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/extracting-lessons.md)
88	(applied by its conversation-extract daily task over captured logs), and the member-side method docs
89	(extract, dedup, pack discovery, and how a project's local packs are identified) live with
90	[grow_with_claudinite](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md).

1	# Evaluating and routing a new item
2	
3	The shared method for three decisions every proposed addition to this corpus must pass through: **is it worthy** of inclusion at all, **which mechanism** should carry it, and — only for prose — **where does it go**. Any routine or person that adds an item — the [growth promote stage](tasks/growth-promote/task.md), an owner-requested retrospective pass, a hand edit — applies this same protocol, so the decision-making lives here once instead of being re-derived per caller.
4	
5	This is a Claudinite-internal doc used by the growth lifecycle (see [the canon-curation README](README.md)): it is **not** part of the mounted corpus and consuming repos do not `@import` it.
6	
7	An "item" is one **distilled, portable rule** — not a transcript, not a narration of what happened. A candidate still phrased as "here's what we did" has not been distilled yet and is below the bar on form alone, before any of the tests below. This doc picks up once a distilled rule exists and decides its fate.
8	
9	## Worthiness — does it earn a place at all
10	
11	The corpus is read read-only by every consuming repo, so a **duplicative** item (already covered) or an **undistilled** one (a story or a truism, not a rule) pollutes shared canon and costs every future reader. The bar guards against *those* — it is **not** a bar on *scope*: an item useful to only one project today can still earn a place (see Portable). Admit an item only when **all** hold:
12	
13	- **Distilled.** It is a single tight rule in the imperative, not a story, a log, or a restatement of a generic truism.
14	- **Portable — would a *future* project benefit?** Not "useful to every project today." An item can help only **one** project right now and still belong here, so long as another project — **especially one with a similar tech stack or process** — would benefit when it arrives. Being specific to a technology or a process is **not** disqualifying: generalize it and route it to that technology's or practice's home. What disqualifies is leaning on *this* project's non-transferable particulars — a product requirement, or a one-off incident in how it happened to call some API. The test, a genuinely hard one: *if another project with a similar tech stack came along, would it benefit from this?* Yes → portable; only-ever-this-product → local.
15	- **Durable and reusable.** It will still apply on a future, unseen task — not a one-off, not a situational detail, not something already implied by an existing rule.
16	- **Readable through the channel it lands in.** A rule whose premise is that the delivery channel
17	  itself failed cannot be carried by that channel. Promote #497 admitted "the tell that the SessionStart
18	  hook did not fire" as pack prose — and pack prose is what that hook delivers, so in the one situation
19	  the rule describes it is not in context to be read. Detecting a channel's own failure belongs in code,
20	  not in the payload the channel carries; reject such an item here rather than rewording it.
21	- **Not already covered.** The insight does not already exist **anywhere** in the corpus, even worded differently or owned by a different file. This is checked against the *entire* corpus, not just the file it would land in — see [Dedupe against the whole corpus](#dedupe-against-the-whole-corpus).
22	
23	Reject on any miss — but the misses that matter are *undistilled*, *already-covered*, or *genuinely one-off*, not merely *narrow*. When you're torn over a real, non-duplicate rule, lean toward **keeping** it — the goal is a broad library. When you're torn over whether something is a duplicate, or a rule at all, leave it out. The failure to avoid is padding the canon with restatements of what's already there; admitting a narrow-but-reusable rule is not that failure.
24	
25	### Dedupe against the whole corpus
26	
27	Before admitting anything, read across the corpus, not only the file you expect to own the item. The same insight is frequently already present under a different heading or in an adjacent group. If it sharpens an **existing** rule, fold it in with a minimal edit rather than adding a second bullet that says nearly the same thing — and never weaken or restate what is already there in the process.
28	
29	## Mechanism triage — prose is the fallback, not the default
30	
31	A worthy item next descends the **promotion ladder** ([../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md) owns it): platform setting (always paired with its verifying check) → PreToolUse hook → conformance check → skill → prose. The *first* rung that can carry the item wins — a rule about repo state becomes a check whose failure message *is* the lesson; a bad action to prevent becomes a guard; a procedure or knowledge with a nameable trigger becomes (or joins) a skill. Only an item none of those can carry — judgment, in-flight behavior, signature-less knowledge — proceeds to the file routing below, and its landing **names that reason** in the promote log so conversion rates stay auditable.
32	
33	**"No universal signature" alone never routes an item to prose.** A rule converts to a check when a *narrow, file-scoped* signature covers the **grounded cases** — the concrete shapes the rule was distilled from — even though no signature covers every conceivable violation. Gate it relevance-first so it stays inert off-target, and document the genuinely signature-less residue in the rule's own comments as out of scope. The prose rung is only for an item whose grounded cases *themselves* have no reliable signature (pure judgment, runtime/in-flight behavior).
34	
35	## Routing — picking the right file (rung-5 items only)
36	
37	Routing is robust when it keys on **stable file groups**, not on the current roster of individual files (which grows over time). The corpus is organized into a few groups, each with its own selection rule:
38	
39	1. **The practice group** — durable, project-agnostic practices, each file a self-contained, reusable unit of know-how the agent applies whenever its subject comes up (engineering, agentic, git/GitHub, testing, investigation, discipline, architecture), partitioned **by kind of practice** with each file owning one recurring subject cluster. This group spans **two folders that differ only by *when* the rule loads**: `always/` for a rule that applies to essentially every task (the index `@`-imports it, so it's force-loaded every session), and `tasks/` for a subject-gated rule read on demand when its trigger fires. Route in two steps: first match the item's *kind* to the file whose cluster already owns that subject; then keep it in `always/` only if it genuinely isn't tied to one kind of task (the rare case — `always/` stays small), otherwise it belongs in `tasks/`. Read the group's own index (the root `CLAUDE.md`) to find the current owner for a kind — never from memory, since the set of clusters can grow.
40	2. **The per-user group** — interaction preferences and trigger phrases, **one file per person**, named for that person's identity. Route an item of this kind to the file for the user it belongs to; it never goes in the practice group.
41	3. **The per-technology group** — practices specific to one technology, **one file per technology**. Route a technology-specific item to that technology's file. When **no pack homes that technology** (not even a stub), the item doesn't land in a loose doc — it **mints a fingerprinted stub pack** (a `packs/<tech>/`, delivered in its own PR), so the next project on that stack self-declares it; [promote](tasks/growth-promote/task.md)'s stub-minting floor and [the generate-project-instructions skill](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md) own the mechanics.
42	
43	Pick **exactly one** owner. If an item plausibly fits two files, choose the single best one — never split one item across files, and never duplicate it into both. The group decides the *axis* (kind, person, or technology); the file within the group is then the one whose existing scope the item falls squarely inside.
44	
45	### When nothing fits
46	
47	An item that matches **no** existing file is **not** a reject signal by itself — a genuinely new category of lesson is meant to be learnable, so a worthy item that no file owns earns its own file. Resolve it in this order:
48	
49	- **Route into an existing owner** when one genuinely fits — the first choice. If the item belongs to a file's cluster and merely sits slightly off-center, a small stretch toward that owner beats spinning up a new file. A new file is for when no existing file's scope genuinely fits, **not** a way to dodge folding into an existing owner.
50	- **Open a new file** when the item clears the [Worthiness](#worthiness--does-it-earn-a-place-at-all) bar in full — distilled, portable, durable and reusable, and not already covered anywhere in the corpus — **and** no existing file's scope genuinely fits it. That is the whole bar: nothing more is required. Do **not** also demand that you expect the cluster to recur, that forcing the item into the closest file would *distort* it, or default to rejecting when the new-file call is a close one — those extra hurdles are dropped. Creating a file obliges registering it where the corpus is indexed and in any routing table, in the **same** change, so it never lands orphaned (see [Keep the write surface bounded](#keep-the-write-surface-bounded)).
51	
52	The loosening above is **only** to the new-cluster hurdle, never to the per-item bar. An item that misses [Worthiness](#worthiness--does-it-earn-a-place-at-all) — a one-off, non-portable or project-specific, a restatement of a generic truism, or already covered anywhere in the corpus — is rejected whether or not a file already exists for it; for the per-item admission decision, the default-to-reject-when-unsure tiebreak still stands.
53	
54	## Keep the write surface bounded
55	
56	Once worthiness and routing are settled, the edit touches **only** the single owning file: add or sharpen one terse rule in that file's existing voice and format, and change nothing else. Do not "improve" unrelated rules while you are in there. The sole exception is the new-file path above, whose surface is itself bounded to the new file plus its index and routing-table registration.

17:- A snapshot/golden test that depends on the current date/time must inject a fixed reference instant, not read the real clock — else a fixed-date fixture silently rots as wall-clock time passes ("this year" becomes "past" next year). Thread the reference time through the code under test, defaulting to the real clock in production. When retrofitting such a rule into an existing fixture suite, pin the reference instant so existing fixtures land on the same side they were authored for — so only the cases that deliberately exercise the new rule change and the diff stays small and reviewable, rather than a sprawling baseline churn that buries the intended change.
21:- Gate a fuzzy quality metric (a coverage %, not a binary pass) behind a high-watermark: refresh the artifact and ratchet the watermark up locally, keep CI read-only (assert against the committed baseline, never rewrite it), and re-baseline by hand only when a deliberate change legitimately moves it — a number that can only climb catches a silent regression without flapping on noise. When the population it covers can *grow* (e.g. new test cases), store the set the watermark was computed over and gate only over the cases shared with it, so a newly added item is excluded rather than dragging the aggregate below the bar; re-anchor the watermark when the set changes. (A single aggregate watermark can then be re-anchored over a regression bundled into the *same* change as a set change — store per-item bars if that must be caught.)
23:- When a snapshot/golden test fails because the output *legitimately* moved (the pixels or bytes changed for a real reason), don't quietly regenerate the baseline to go green — an unreviewed baseline change is an unreviewed behavior change. Surface the diff (committed **expected**, newly-rendered **actual**, highlighted **diff**) and get owner approval before re-baselining; until then keep the *reverted* baseline committed so the branch honestly shows the test red-pending — never commit the new baseline first.
24:- When a test asserts exact values extracted from a captured artifact (a cached page, a recorded response), record and commit the artifact *first*, then read the expected values off the committed file — don't hand-write the expectations from memory or a live view and hope they match. Guessing the value desyncs the test from the real fixture; reading it off the committed bytes can't.
25:- A test that maintains a committed artifact should regenerate it into the working tree deterministically (no timestamps, so an unchanged run yields no diff) and skip the write under CI — never shell out to git from a test. Commit the artifact through the normal review flow, like a snapshot.
27:- To image-golden a surface your code **injects into a host page** (a control mounted into a third-party toolbar), render it against a **committed capture of the real host DOM with its computed styles flattened inline** — the deterministic rasterizer reads only inline styles, and the host's own stylesheet is not yours to ship. Mount it with the **shipped injector** (so the golden proves the placement, not a hand-placed copy), and name the model's boundary honestly: substituted icon-font glyphs, an approximated host chrome (a captured sample is spec, not folklore — the origin lesson of a supported-targets matrix).

Weight the repo's own shipped-working behavior over external or general claims (web search, blogs) when they conflict: prior working code is a real run; a stale external claim isn't.

1	# Scheduled tasks — the per-project scheduling mechanism
2	
3	How a repo's recurring Claudinite work runs (per-project-scheduling
4	[DESIGN](../../docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md), issue #394). A repo
5	schedules **itself**: a vendored hourly **scheduler Action**
6	(`.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml`) evaluates each task's precondition
7	in code and dispatches agent work as `ready-for-agent` `[claudinite-task]`
8	issues, which a per-repo **executor routine** (fired by that label event) runs.
9	The engine is vendored under `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/`; the basics
10	pack owns the conformance guards for the surfaces a repo authors around it —
11	scheduling is baseline Claudinite discipline, present wherever basics is
12	declared (everywhere), not an opt-in feature.
13	
14	The checks below are the doctrine's enforcement; the phased rollout (and the
15	retirement of the legacy central planner it replaces) lives in
16	[MIGRATION.md](../../docs/per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md).
17	
18	## What the checks guard
19	
20	- **The scheduler workflow is a thin shim.** The vendored
21	  `claudinite-scheduler.yml` carries a single **hourly** cron on a repo-hashed
22	  minute constrained to **:10–:50** (the one repo-specific value in the stub —
23	  `engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs`, a pure function of the repo full name that
24	  bootstrap stamps in and baselining re-derives), a `concurrency` group, a
25	  `workflow_dispatch` trigger, and a call into the vendored engine entry — no logic of its own
26	  (schema and behaviour changes ride the vendor refresh, not workflow edits). It
27	  is the repo's **only** cron. Recurring work that had its own cron'd workflow
28	  becomes a **task**, and that workflow is deleted — its steps move into the
29	  task's worker. Don't keep it as a dispatch-only workflow for the task to fire:
30	  that is two files and two edit sites for one job, and a workflow whose only
31	  caller is the thing that replaced it. (A workflow that must run *as an Action*
32	  for something a task cannot reach — an Actions-only secret, say — is the
33	  exception, and even then the task owns the schedule.) Off-band or multiple
34	  crons, or a missing concurrency/dispatch guard, break staggering, double-run
35	  safety, or manual runs.
36	
37	- **Every task declaration carries the full contract.** A `tasks/<name>/task.mjs`
38	  default-exports `id` (matching its directory), `frequency` (`hourly | daily-2h
39	  | daily-1h | daily | daily+1h | weekly | monthly`), `precondition_signals` (the collector
40	  vocabulary), `agent_model` (`opus | sonnet | haiku | none`), `expected_outcome` (`none |
41	  open-pr | merged-pr`), and a `precondition`. An agentic task (`agent_model !==
42	  none`) also carries `agent_instructions`, the worker file the agent reads; a
43	  `none` task runs no agent, so the field is not applicable and is omitted. The
44	  scheduler and executor read agent_model/expected_outcome/frequency from this file — never from the dispatch
45	  issue — so an illegal or missing value means a task never fires, fires wrong,
46	  or writes past its declared ceiling. The same contract
47	  (`engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs`) is re-validated at run time, so the
48	  static and runtime views can't drift. Optionally, `session_scope` (`self` default
49	  | `fleet`) declares whether the task reaches only its own repo or across the
50	  owner's repos: a `fleet` task dispatches to the `ready-for-agent-fleet` label so a
51	  distinct, broader-scoped executor runs it, keeping the fleet-wide session grant
52	  off every ordinary project's `ready-for-agent` (self) executor.
53	
54	- **Every run is bounded.** An agentic task (`agent_model !== none`) declares
55	  `agent_execution_timeout` — seconds bounding the agentic run
56	  (agent-preprocessing [DESIGN](../../docs/agent-preprocessing/DESIGN.md) §2, §6).
57	  There is no platform wall-clock kill for a launched executor session, so the
58	  bound is best-effort: the executor surfaces it into the subagent's brief ("fail
59	  after N minutes") and the stale-`agent-running` backstop catches a dead session.
60	  Set it generously — extreme protection against a runaway, not a scheduling knob.
61	
62	- **A task says which repo secrets it needs.** Preprocessing runs Action-side, so
63	  repo Actions secrets are reachable there and nowhere else in a task's life (an
64	  executor session carries none). A task lists what it needs in `required_secrets`;
65	  the wiring converge stamps each name into the scheduler workflow, so a worker
66	  reads it as ordinary environment, and baselining asks the owner (one standing
67	  issue) for any the repo hasn't configured. The adoption interview's posture, not
68	  a gate — nothing fails; the task that needs the secret just doesn't work yet. The
69	  consequence worth designing around: **a workflow that exists only to hold a
70	  secret is redundant** — fold its work into the task's preprocessing rather than
71	  dispatching and polling a second workflow from an agent.
72	
73	Both guards are **relevance-first**: inert until their artifact exists, so
74	on a repo with neither artifact they are a no-op.
75	
76	## The task folder
77	
78	One directory per task — `<pack>/tasks/<name>/` — holding **`task.mjs`** (the
79	self-contained declaration + `precondition(signals, config)`, the eligibility
80	gate as pure code) beside **`task.md`** (the worker spec the executing agent
81	follows), plus any deterministic helpers. The precondition both asserts
82	need-to-run and pre-decides scope: its `context` lines land verbatim in the
83	dispatch issue as binding constraints the agent may not re-litigate. `agent_model:
84	none` replaces the worker doc with an inline `.mjs` the scheduler runs directly —
85	no agent, no issue. This is the scheduled-task shape of the unattended-agents
86	routine-folder convention; the issue-driven-dispatch security rule (the issue is
87	data, the task path is code-validated, agent_model/expected_outcome come from the repo) lives
88	with that skill's agent practices.
89	
90	## The dispatch labels are a scheduler vocabulary
91	
92	**Both ready labels are triggers**, so they belong on dispatch issues alone — never put
93	`ready-for-agent` or `ready-for-agent-fleet` on an ordinary issue, from a task or by hand.
94	Applying one starts an executor session that will find no valid dispatch and stop.
95	`agent-running` and `needs-human` carry no trigger and are the right vocabulary for a task
96	that needs to mark an issue as claimed or handed to a human; a task reusing them owns their
97	whole lifecycle on its own issues, since the scheduler's stale-claim backstop only converges
98	`[claudinite-task]` dispatch issues.
99	
100	Which ready label a task dispatches under follows from its `session_scope`, and the executor
101	session started by that label is the one with the matching reach — a `fleet` task's session
102	has the owner's repos in its sources, a `self` task's has this repo alone. The task declares
103	the scope; nothing downstream re-decides it.
104	
105	## A dormant project runs nothing
106	
107	A project nobody is working on declares itself dormant in `.claudinite-checks.json`:
108	
109	```json
110	"dormant": true
111	```
112	
113	The scheduler stops before evaluating anything; the [fleet sweeps](../sheepdog/README.md)
114	skip it; sessions are unaffected. Delete it to wake.

########## .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md
# Growth — discover canon packs (the fleet sweep)

One weekly pass over **every member**: read what the fleet is actually built on, subtract what the shared canon already homes, and open a PR **for the owner to approve** authoring the pack that is missing. Declared only by Claudinite, so it runs **once, centrally**, never per project.

This is the only thing that notices a technology in use across the fleet with **no canon pack**. Its per-repo namesake in [grow_with_claudinite](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md) is the other side of the same line: that one authors a repo's **own local** packs and is barred from re-creating what a canon pack homes. It cannot close a canon gap; you can, and only you.

**Why central.** One run sees every member, so **first-sight dedup is free**: the third member using a technology is recognised as the same gap as the first, in the same pass, with no cross-run state and no chance of three repos each proposing the same pack.

You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent-fleet` issue whose **Context section is binding scope**: it names the exact members to sweep. Work exactly that list — the fleet enumeration already happened in the precondition; **do not enumerate the fleet yourself or widen past the Context**. Finding nothing unhomed is a perfectly good, common outcome.

The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`open-pr`**: a new canon pack is read by every repo that declares it, so it opens a PR and **never arms auto-merge** — the owner approves it.

## Conventions used in this doc

- **GitHub access is MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`). You are outside each member repo — read its files over the API (get-file-contents, never a cross-repo checkout; the sandbox has no cross-repo git). The Claudinite PR is opened over MCP too.
- **`main`** stands for Claudinite's default branch.
- **The canon shelf** is Claudinite's own `packs/` tree — the packs every member can declare.

## What each run does

### 1. Manifest each member's stack

For each member named in Context, catalogue what it is built on, exactly as the per-repo task's [manifest step](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md) specifies — the same three axes, the same per-item fields, the same **never infer from "projects like this usually…"** rule, the same comprehensive-over-concise bias. That step owns the method; do not re-derive or re-state it here. The only adaptation: you read the member over the API rather than a working checkout, and you keep one manifest **per member**, tagged with the repo it came from.

Do not consult the canon shelf yet, and decide nothing about packs — this step only observes.

### 2. Fold the members into one fleet view

Merge the per-member manifests into a single list of technologies, keyed by the technology, each carrying **which members use it** and at what prominence. This fold is the whole reason the task is central: the same technology seen in four members is **one** entry, recognised on first sight, so there is no cross-run dedup state and no duplicate proposal.

Drop anything no member uses at `core` or `supporting` prominence — a technology only some member's vestigial config mentions has taught the fleet nothing.

### 3. Find the canon gap

Hold the fleet view against the **canon shelf**. A candidate is a technology (or a domain the fleet shares) that:

- **no canon pack homes** — and, per the per-repo task's rule, **a stub pack counts as homed**: if `packs/` already has any pack owning it, the gap is closed. The action for a member using a homed technology without declaring its pack is to note that ("member X should declare pack Y"), never to author a second pack; **and**
- carries **real, portable working knowledge** the members actually demonstrate — a build/config gotcha, a toolchain rule, a procedure that recurs across them. Judge worthiness by the bar [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns; don't restate its gates.

Prefer a candidate **more than one member** uses — that is the evidence a pack is portable rather than one repo's local business. A single-member technology can still qualify when the knowledge is plainly general, but it is the weaker case, and the per-repo task already covers the local-pack answer.

### 4. Author the pack — from the members' real usage

Author `packs/<name>/` using the pack-writing mechanics [the generate-project-instructions skill](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md) owns — descend the promotion ladder, add the `marker`/`detect` fingerprint when the technology carries a reliable one (`detect: null` otherwise), write `RULES.md`/`pack.mjs`/`README.md`, and add its `packs/README.md` index row. Apply that method; do not re-derive it.

Two rules from the per-repo task carry over unchanged, and are the ones this task most easily breaks because it is writing from *other* repos' evidence:

- **Ground every rule in a member's real files, and cite which member.** Never author from imagination.
- **Never pad** with speculative best-practice rules the evidence doesn't demonstrate, and **never open an empty stub to fill later**. A small honest pack beats a padded one; a rule you can't ground, you don't write.

Strip the member (names, paths, and product concepts stay in the origin repo — a canon pack is written as if no particular repo existed); a technology mention is the point, a *product* mention is a defect.

**One pack per PR.** A new pack earns its own review surface, so a run that finds two gaps opens two PRs.

### 5. Open the PR

Open a PR against `main` on a per-run-unique branch — never a direct push. Write surface is **`packs/` only**: the new pack's files and the `packs/README.md` index row. Don't "improve" unrelated packs while you're in there. Keep every commit and PR terse, and **put the issue reference in the commit message** (`Refs #<n>` for the tracker below), in the commit itself and not only the PR body.

### 6. Log the run to the tracker

The standing log is the issue titled exactly **`Claudinite tracker: Discover Canon Packs`**.

- **Find it by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number** (a bare number can dangle).
- **Create it already closed if missing. Never open, close, or reopen it** — its state carries no meaning; only the log does.
- Log every run as a **dated comment**: the members swept; each pack authored (technology, the members that evidenced it, the rungs its rules landed on); each "member X should declare existing pack Y" note; and, for a candidate you rejected, its name and why. "Nothing unhomed this run" is worth a line too.

## What this task must never do

- **Never widen past the Context member list**, and **never touch a member repo** — this task only reads members and writes the Claudinite PR.
- **Never author a pack for a technology the canon already homes** — a stub counts as homed; note the "declare the existing pack" action instead.
- **Never author from imagination or pad, and never open an empty stub** — every rule traces to a named member's real files.
- **Never write a member's product names, paths, or concepts into a canon pack** — that is the local-pack answer, and it belongs to the per-repo task.
- **Never write outside `packs/`** — no engine, no docs, no member-side change.
- **Run on `opus`** — every step is a judgment call (is this technology genuinely unhomed, has the fleet earned a shared pack for it, what does the evidence actually support), and you are authoring from *other* repos' evidence with no owner able to re-derive each call. This task declares `agent_model: opus`.
########## .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/tasks/growth-promote/task.md
# Growth — promote lessons into the canon (the central stage)

The [growth lifecycle](../../README.md)'s central stage: read the target members' local packs, lift the portable lessons into the shared canon, and open a PR against the canon's default branch **for the owner to approve**. Declared only by the Claudinite home repo, so it runs **once, centrally**, never per project.

You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding scope**: it names the exact target members (those whose local packs changed in the window). Work exactly that list — the fleet enumeration already happened in the precondition; **do not enumerate the fleet yourself or widen past the Context**.

The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`open-pr`**: promotion is the **judgment gate before shared canon**. It opens a PR and **never arms auto-merge** — the owner approves it. But don't lean on that review as the portability check: [extract](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-extract/task.md) stays project-specific by design, so it's no second opinion, and the owner can't re-derive every portability call. This task's judgment is the real thing between a bad rule and every project that reads the canon — keep the bar high (dedupe against the whole corpus; default to reject when unsure).

## Conventions used in this doc

- **GitHub access is MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`). You are outside each member repo — read its files over the API (get-file-contents, never a cross-repo checkout; the sandbox has no cross-repo git). The canon PR is opened over MCP too.
- **A member's local packs** are everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename window) — its own packs, never the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under `.claudinite/`.
- **`main`** stands for the canon's default branch.

## What each run does

### 1. Read the target members' local **packs**

For each member named in Context, read its **local packs**. The candidate pool is a local pack's captured knowledge — its `RULES.md` **prose** AND its own **checks** (a `<pack>/*.mjs` rule module — its id, description, and failure message *are* a captured, enforceable lesson; the strongest promotion lifts it to a **canon check**, generalized, reusing the [prose-to-checks](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) mechanics — or to canon prose when it doesn't generalize to a check). **Out of scope, staying put:** a lesson deliberately placed as a **code comment at its call site**, a project's task scripts, product source, and config. Never promote from product source. A genuinely portable rule that looks trapped in a code comment was mis-placed at extract time — leave it for a future extract pass to re-home into a pack. You don't need to tell new from old — the dedup step drops anything the canon already carries. No barrier holds tonight's extracts: read whatever is already **merged** on each member's default branch; anything landing mid-run is tomorrow's input.

### 2. Generalize each candidate — *before* judging whether it belongs

Generalize first, then decide worthiness — never the reverse. The act of generalizing is itself the portability probe — a rule that goes vacuous when lifted, or only makes sense with its project's context, isn't portable; leave it local. Work the rule standalone (origin naming and grouping carry no weight); strip the project (names, files, example stay in the origin repo — promote the distilled rule only); a **technology** mention isn't a disqualifier (lift it to the broadest scope that stays true — tech-specific is fine, *product*-specific is not); decide tool-vs-process and frame it for that home.

### 3. Then judge worthiness — deduped against the *entire* corpus

Holding the generalized rule, decide if it earns a place by the bar [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns (don't restate its gates). Lean **inclusive** — keep anything a future project could use — but be strict about **duplication**: dedupe against **every** corpus doc, not only the one you'd expect to own it.

### 4. Triage the mechanism, then route

- **Descend the promotion ladder first** ([item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md)'s mechanism triage). Prose is the fallback, not the default: a lesson a check can carry is **authored as the check** in this PR — the rule module in the right pack, the failure message carrying the generalized lesson, **plus a fixture test proving it fires** on a violating input and stays quiet on a clean one. When a confident detection-plus-fixture can't be authored unattended, land the lesson as prose **and** open a tagged conformance-backlog issue — never a silently-shipped broken check.
- **Route** each prose rule to its **one** owning doc ([item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns the placement); match its voice and format; pick exactly one owner, never split or duplicate.
- **A technology with no home → mint a fingerprinted stub pack, in its own PR**, reusing the pack-writing mechanics [the generate-project-instructions skill](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md) owns — `packs/<tech>/` with `pack.mjs` (add the `marker`/`detect` fingerprint when the technology carries a reliable one, else `detect: null`), a `RULES.md` seeded from the lesson, a `README.md`, and its `packs/README.md` index row. A minted pack ships in its **own** PR, split from the run's lesson-promotion PR (a new pack earns its own review surface). Never mint from imagination and never park an empty one to fill later — a pack minted here is populated from the *real, portable lesson* that justified it. Do not pad it with speculative rules no project earned — the "written from imagination, not distilled from worked examples" failure; an ungroundable rule isn't written. (Authoring a *fuller* pack from a technology's usage across the whole fleet — rather than a single lesson — is the per-repo pack-discovery task's job, not this floor's.) The follow-ups a fresh stub invites — enriching it from known best practices, triaging which skills it should require, spinning up dependent/aspect packs — are **not** automated here: note them for the owner and leave them to a later, deliberate pass.
- **Write it terse — when + what.** State the relevance (*when* it applies) and the rule (*what* to do); add a *why* only to flag severity, in a few words.
- **Bounded write surface — `packs/`/`skills/` only** (CI-enforced on the PR). Edit only the one owning doc — or, for a check-conversion, only the new rule module, its registration in the pack registry, and its fixture test. Don't "improve" unrelated rules while you're in there. The two bounded exceptions (both within `packs/`): the new-doc path [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns, and minting a stub pack.
- **Open a PR against `main`** on a per-run-unique branch — one PR for the whole run's accepted lessons (a minted stub is the exception: its own PR). Never a direct push. Keep every commit and PR terse. **Put the issue reference in the commit message** (`Refs #<n>` for the tracker below) — the `basics` `task-lifecycle` check reds CI on a promote commit that cites none.

### 5. Log the run to the tracker

Append a dated comment for every run that promoted at least one lesson, and for any notable rejection.

## Tracking issue

The standing self-improvement log is the issue titled exactly **`Claudinite tracker: Promote to Canon`**.

- **Find it by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number** (a bare number can dangle).
- **Create it already closed if missing. Never open, close, or reopen it** — its state carries no meaning; only the log does.
- Log each run as a **dated comment** — not a sub-issue, so history accumulates in one scrollable feed — the date, and per lesson: the origin repo, the **ladder rung it landed on** (check id / skill / owning doc, with the named reason when prose was the fallback), and the generalized rule (or, for a notable rejection, the reason and the existing rule that already covers it).

## What this task must never do

- **Never mine outside a local pack** — product source, task scripts, code comments, and config are out of scope; only a local pack's `RULES.md` prose and its own check modules are candidates.
- **Never promote a product-specific or one-off item** — it stays in that project's local packs.
- **Never weaken, restate, or duplicate an existing rule** — fold a genuine sharpening in per [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) instead.
- **Never widen past the Context member list**, and **never touch a member repo** — this task only reads members and writes the canon PR.
- **Run on `opus`** — every step is a judgment call (portability, duplication, ownership, how to generalize without distorting), and a downgraded model ships a plausible-but-wrong *acceptance* the owner's review is least likely to catch. This task declares `agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.

# Migrations — archive records past their TTL

**This task runs no agent.** It is `agent_model: none` with `agent_preprocessing: node worker.mjs`, so the whole pass is the deterministic [`worker.mjs`](worker.mjs) the scheduler runs as a subprocess. This file is the human-facing record of what that worker does; there is no dispatch issue and no subagent.

## What it does

Every migration record whose age has passed the **7-day TTL** (since its `landed` date) moves from `migrations/active_migrations/` to the canon-only `migrations/migrations-old/` archive, delivered as **one PR**. No fleet enumeration, no fleet PAT — the decision is a pure age comparison over the canon's own records (`migrationsPastTtl` in `migrations/registry.mjs`, unit-tested there).

## Archival, not deletion

Moving a record to `migrations-old/` keeps it working — it is **not** a delete:

- **It still applies.** `loadMigrations()` reads **both** folders, so a **dormant project** — one that fell behind and only now baselines — still gets an aged migration applied when baselining converges its mount out of a fresh canon clone. The archive is the durable backfill source for the long tail.
- **It stops shipping.** The archive is **canon-only** — the vendored consumer mount ships only `active_migrations/`. A project up to speed on migrations therefore carries few-to-none of these locally; it already applied them within the TTL window.
- **Its check-tolerance ends.** `migrationActive()` scans only `active_migrations/`, so a migration's legacy-shape tolerance ends when it ages out — every up-to-date repo converged within the TTL, and a dormant one is converged by the apply pass *before* its checks run.

## Delivery

The move is staged on a stable `claudinite/archive-migrations` branch and delivered as one PR (amended in place across runs) over the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` — the canon's own CI validates the move before it lands. Because the record still applies from its new home, the move is behavior-preserving; the PR is safe to merge once green.

1	# Extracting lessons from a working session
2	
3	> **Scope: a single agent ↔ user conversation.** This doc is the **method** for mining one
4	> working session's *dialogue and the actions taken in it* for improvements. It is **not** the
5	> growth extract ([the growth-extract task](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) that mines **issues, PRs, and commits** over repo
6	> history — that routine never sees a conversation. Its two callers: the
7	> [conversation-extract daily task](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md), which applies it to **captured**
8	> conversation logs — where the friction signals below (a clarifying round-trip, a backtrack, a
9	> wait you sat through) survive with their timestamps — and an owner's occasional plain-words
10	> ask for a retrospective over the live session.
11	
12	Portable guidance for mining an agent ↔ user session — a Claude Code web session, a CLI run, a
13	captured conversation log — for durable improvements: read the conversation and convert its
14	friction into changes that make the **next** run faster, clearer, and less dependent on human
15	feedback.
16	
17	Run the reflection on a **capable model.** Extraction is mechanical, but deciding *what clears
18	the bar* is a judgment call a weaker model fails silently — it ships a plausible-but-wrong
19	"lesson" where a capable model correctly bails (see
20	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md), "Match the agent model
21	to the judgment it must make"). The terse rules that *govern* the pass — run it, plus the
22	separate efficiency analysis — also live there; this doc is the how-to.
23	
24	## The goal
25	
26	Every pass optimizes for one outcome: **the next run needs less.** Less clarification, less
27	rework, less waiting, less human steering. Read the session not as "what did we accomplish" but
28	as "where did this cost more than it should have, and what durable change removes that cost
29	next time." If a pass can't name a concrete next-time saving, it found nothing — and that's
30	fine (see [No new lessons](#no-new-lessons-is-a-valid--and-common--result)).
31	
32	## When it runs
33	
34	Routinely, in the [conversation-extract daily task](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md) over each captured
35	log (a fresh pass within a day of capture, a final hindsight pass before retention deletes the
36	log) — the standard path. If an owner asks in plain words for a retrospective over the live
37	session, apply the same method and deliver the capture as a branch + PR **for a human to review**,
38	never one that self-merges (the nightly auto-merges its own PR per its own doc; a live retrospective
39	wants human eyes). **Never
40	reflect-and-edit unprompted in the middle of a task** — it interrupts the work; the owner
41	decides when a session is done enough to mine.
42	
43	## What to look for — the friction signals
44	
45	Read the conversation end to end and hunt for these signatures. Each marks a place the loop
46	cost more than necessary, and each converts to a specific durable fix.
47	
48	### 1. Misunderstandings between agent and user
49	
50	The signs: a clarifying-question round-trip; the user correcting an assumption ("no, I
51	meant…"); the agent building the wrong thing and reworking it; the user restating the same
52	request; an `AskUserQuestion` whose answer was, in hindsight, the obvious default.
53	
54	**Convert to:** encode the resolved understanding so the next agent never has to ask. Every
55	question the user answered is a candidate **default**; every correction is a candidate
56	**convention or glossary entry**; a recurring wrong assumption is a candidate **confirm-first
57	checkpoint placed earlier**, or a clearer doc the agent reads cold and gets right the first
58	time. The test of a good fix: next time the agent proceeds correctly **without the round-trip**.
59	
60	### 2. Suboptimal agent actions
61	
62	The signs: the agent took an approach then backtracked; did redundant or repeated work; re-ran
63	a command that had already failed for a knowable reason; reached for a heavy tool where a light
64	one fit; reinvented something the codebase already provided; re-read a file it had just written
65	to "verify"; missed an existing convention and had it corrected in review.
66	
67	**Convert to:** a rule pointing at the right approach or tool, a pointer to the existing
68	helper/convention so it's found first, or a **footgun note placed where it'll be read.** Place
69	it by where the trap is hit, not in a central bucket: a gotcha from **misusing a specific API,
70	class, or library goes as a comment right at the usage site** — next to the call itself, where
71	the next editor of that line sees it — never collected into a centralized gotchas list.
72	Co-locate it in a file's own header comment when the trap spans the whole file and you'd only
73	hit it *while editing that file*. Reserve a central gotchas doc for what no single usage site
74	owns: a trap you could hit *without* reading the relevant file (a mistake of omission), or a
75	cross-cutting invariant. The test: next time the agent takes the good path first, not after a
76	detour.
77	
78	### 3. Long wall-time waits — and measure them
79	
80	The signs: independent operations run **serially** that had no dependency and could have been
81	parallel; a padded fixed `sleep` that over- or under-shot; a process **waited out after its
82	result was already in hand**; blind long polling; re-running a check (e.g. CI) that was already
83	green.
84	
85	**Measure, don't hand-wave.** Quantify the wait with real wall-clock numbers and separate the
86	kinds of time — compute (a compile, a test/render run) vs. genuine **idle waiting** (sleeps,
87	polling, a finished process not yet killed). A captured log carries per-entry timestamps and
88	per-message token usage, so the numbers are computable, not estimated. A fix is only credible
89	against numbers; name the **single highest-leverage change** that shortens it, or conclude it
90	was already optimal.
91	
92	**Convert to:** a batch/parallelize rule, a poll-with-rolling-backoff instead of a blind sleep,
93	kill-the-process-once-its-output-is-in-hand, or merge-on-an-already-green-check. (These are the
94	subject of the standing **efficiency analysis** in
95	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md) — fold a wall-time
96	finding into that frame rather than re-deriving it.) The test: same result, less wall clock, no
97	loss of quality.
98	
99	## Encode the questions the user keeps asking
100	
101	The single highest-leverage move for **less human feedback**: the questions a user asks
102	*repeatedly* are a checklist the agent should run **itself.** If the user keeps asking "how
103	many processes ran — could it be fewer?", "what took longest?", "did you kill it the moment its
104	work was done?", stop waiting to be asked — fold those exact questions into a **standing
105	self-check the agent answers proactively** at the end of the relevant work, and close with a
106	terse verdict (a concrete change, or an explicit "already optimal"). Each recurring question
107	converted this way is one the user never has to ask again — and it's where a *measured*
108	retrospective comes from: the user's recurring efficiency questions, answered pre-emptively,
109	with numbers.
110	
111	## From signal to lesson — the bar
112	
113	A friction signal is only worth writing down when the fix is **durable, reusable, and
114	generalizable beyond this one session.** Before adding anything:
115	
116	- **Dedupe ruthlessly** against the existing packs — a lesson already covered (even worded
117	  differently, even in another pack, even enforced by a check) is not a new lesson.
118	- **Route to the local pack that owns it, and prefer the strongest mechanism** — the **local
119	  promotion ladder**, at the project's own level. A project's capture surface is its **local
120	  packs** (`.claudinite/local_packs/<pack>/`): pick the pack whose territory the lesson belongs
121	  to, then a deterministic rule becomes a **check** in that pack's `rules` (its failure message
122	  *is* the lesson; ship it with a red-first fixture), an activity-scoped procedure becomes a
123	  **pack skill**, and only what neither can carry lands as terse **prose** in the pack's
124	  `RULES.md`. Write more checks and less prose — a check relieves every session's context
125	  completely where prose only relocates it. A gotcha tied to one call site still goes as a
126	  comment at that site (above), not into any pack. When no pack's scope fits and the lesson
127	  warrants segregation, a new local pack is a self-contained directory drop.
128	- **Promote what's portable.** A lesson true for projects beyond this one belongs in shared,
129	  cross-project canon, not stuck in one repo's local packs — the growth lifecycle's promote
130	  stage lifts it there centrally; capture it well locally and let promote generalize whatever
131	  travels.
132	- **One-offs don't qualify.** A situational detail, a restatement of a generic truism, or
133	  something already implied by an existing rule is below the bar.
134	
135	## "No new lessons" is a valid — and common — result
136	
137	Most sessions yield nothing durable, and that's the expected outcome. Say so and write nothing
138	rather than padding the docs to look productive: a spurious or duplicative "lesson" pollutes
139	the canon and costs every future reader. **Default to no edit when unsure** — the bar is a
140	genuinely new, reusable insight, not a diary of what happened.

1	# grow_with_claudinite
2	
3	Opt into the **growth lifecycle** — declaring this pack enrolls a repo in contributing its hard-won
4	lessons up to the shared Claudinite canon, and in pruning its local packs once the canon owns them.
5	Seeded by default (`--init` + the one-time `grow-with-claudinite-seed` baseline migration for the

9	lessons into its local packs, and pruning them once the shared canon covers them. The central
10	**promote** stage — which lifts portable lessons up into the shared canon — is a home-only duty
11	that runs canon-side, not a repo-side task, so it lives outside this pack.

17	|---|---|---|

27	
28	## The conversation lifecycle — capture in-session, extract in a daily task, retention
29	
30	The pack also owns **extraction from working sessions** — the conversation-side sibling of the
31	issues/PRs/commits extract above, replacing the old in-session post-merge lessons pass. The two
32	halves split by what each needs: **capture** needs the live session transcript, so it runs
33	in-session (at merge, and again when the session ends); **extraction** only reads the
34	already-pushed logs, so it is an ordinary
35	scheduled task with `growth-extract`'s access model — the logs branch is *in the repo*,
36	so reading it, committing lessons to local packs, and pruning are plain local git on the working
37	tree; only posting the summary on the issue uses the GitHub MCP tools.
38	
39	1. **Capture — a step in the merge-to-main skill** (in-session, where the transcript lives).
40	   Right after a merge lands:
41	   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
42	   (in the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`).
43	   Deterministic, seconds; it bundles the session transcript (sidechains inline, timestamp

45	   minus a short named allowlist of structural values, plus known credential stores — is
46	   redacted wherever it appears, with credential-shape patterns as the backstop; a secret the
47	   session itself transformed is beyond any static scrub, and push protection is the last
48	   net), and pushes one file per **capture event** onto the orphan **`conversation-logs`**
49	   branch: `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, commits marked `[skip ci]`.
50	   **Delta-aware, keyed on the session id:** every capture pushes only the entries after this
